# aLogin.exe catalog

<!-- Generated by tools/decompile/catalog.py from var/decompiled; edit SUBSYSTEMS there, not this file. -->

The decompiled client (WLRI build `ca19ee087b60`) has **12,130 functions** and **937 classes**. The Go port cites **658** of those functions by address. Regions are the address ranges of the decompiler's unit table; their names in `meta/units.txt` are shifted, so each is identified by its classes and strings. *Cited* is a lower bound of ported code. The plan is in [CLIENT_ROADMAP.md](CLIENT_ROADMAP.md); machine-readable data is in `client-inventory.json`.

Statuses: **ported** (in use, details remain), **partial** (core in place, features missing), **started** (a few pieces), **todo**, **replaced** (a Go or Ebitengine facility stands in; not ported function by function).

<a id="assets"></a>
### Asset decryption and data files

Status **ported**; 47 functions, 4 cited. Go: internal/clientassets, internal/assets, internal/clientbundle, internal/clientruntime, internal/clientimage, internal/clientfs.

JMA/JXAN decryption, .wmg data; editable exports compile incrementally into separate ZIP64 core/world/sprite/audio packs, binary terrain/event/object records and lazy sprite metadata with build-time palette matching; PNG dimensions and JSON/frame references are validated. Non-sprite images compile into lossless, independently readable tiles with native color preparation, empty-border trimming, small-image atlas packing, content deduplication and byte-bounded LRU caching. Large map backgrounds draw only visible tiles; per-image dependencies preserve incremental builds. Loose data/ remains a development input.

| 83 | 10e9cc–10eeec | 10 | 2 | TCY_WmgData |

<a id="graphics"></a>
### Graphics backend (DelphiX, DirectDraw, JPEG, rodraw2)

Status **replaced**; 670 functions, 2 cited. Go: client/wlo/surface, client/wlo/render, Ebitengine.

TDXDraw/DirectDraw surfaces use native-compatible Ebitengine GPU render targets by default, with a CPU RGB565 compatibility path. GPU shaders preserve colour keys, integer alpha/light/scaling and palette recolouring; UI/text blits can batch. Visible map tiles and a shared bounded texture cache serve all sessions, with GPU composition/previews and explicit capture-only readbacks. Graphics and full-client frame parity tests verify the replacement.
